NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday inaugurated the Alluri Sitarama Raju International Airport at Bhogapuram in Andhra Pradesh 's Vizianagaram district, a nearly Rs 5,000 crore project that the state government says will transform North Andhra into a major economic and industrial hub.The PM was accorded a grand ceremonial welcome, with around 13,500 tribal women performing the traditional Dhimsa dance. It has been designed to handle six million passengers annually in its first phase, with a long-term expansion plan to increase capacity to 40 million passengers a year. During the visit, Naidu and Union minister Ram Mohan Naidu also briefed the Prime Minister on the airport's features and future development plans. Meanwhile, the PM will inaugurate e Swami Vivekananda Cultural Youth Centre - Viveka Smaraka at Sri Ramakrishna Ashrama in Karnataka's Mysuru at 3:30 PM

Article Title: FSSAI cracks down on three firms over food safety violations
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) has launched a fresh enforcement drive against food business operators, issuing a product recall, suspending a manufacturing licence and prohibiting the sale of a health supplement over serious violations of food safety regulations.In one action, FSSAI ordered M/s Sun Organic Industries Pvt Ltd to immediately recall its Wonderland Raisins after regulatory testing found pesticide residues exceeding the prescribed limits. Samples tested at both the National Food Laboratory, Ghaziabad, and the Referral Laboratory, NIFTEM-K, were declared "unsafe" under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006. The company has been directed to recall the entire batch from the market and submit periodic recall status reports.In a separate action, the food regulator suspended the licence of Dior Pharmaceuticals' Nutraceutical Manufacturing Unit with immediate effect after an inspection revealed major and critical non-compliances. According to FSSAI, the unit failed to comply with several regulatory and hygiene requirements, including inadequate quality management systems and deficiencies in manufacturing practices.FSSAI also issued a prohibition order against M/s Vatave Health Care, banning the manufacture, storage, distribution and sale of its Folineuro Syrup (Folinic Acid Syrup). The regulator said the product was marketed as a nutritional food supplement with misleading claims related to brain function despite not complying with provisions of the Food Safety and Standards Act and the Food Safety and Standards (Health Supplements, Nutraceuticals, Food for Special Dietary Use, Food for Special Medical Purpose, Functional Food and Novel Food) Regulations, 2016.The regulator said the actions were taken to protect consumers and ensure compliance with food safety laws. It warned that violations of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, would invite strict legal and penal action.
Article Summary: The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) has launched a fresh enforcement drive against food business operators. The regulator has issued a product recall, suspended a manufacturing licence and prohibited the sale of a health supplement over serious violations of food safety regulations.

Article Title: 'Same people who litter here, use dustbin abroad': Bombay HC on civic sense
Article Text:
The court stressed that maintaining cleanliness is a fundamental duty and called for strict action against offenders. (Generative image)

NEW DELHI: The Bombay high court on Friday came down heavily on Indians who litter public places at home but follow cleanliness rules abroad, saying the same people who "throw garbage on the road without batting an eyelid" in India ensure to put "even a small chocolate wrapper" in the dustbin abroad.The court stressed that maintaining cleanliness is a fundamental duty and called for strict action against offenders.A bench of Justices G S Kulkarni and Aarti Sathe made the observations while hearing a batch of petitions over pollution, foul odour, gas emissions and health hazards linked to the Kanjurmarg dumping ground in Mumbai.The judges said public participation was essential to keeping the city clean and urged civic authorities to enforce the rules without hesitation."If a person wants a clean environment, then he or she has a corresponding fundamental duty towards society to maintain cleanliness. We want the civic officials to be ruthless in taking action," the court said according to news agency PTI.Expressing concern over people's attitude towards public cleanliness, the bench said citizens often behave differently once they leave India."We have to sensitise our citizens. Here, a person will throw garbage on the road without batting an eyelid, but these same people, when abroad, will strictly avoid such behaviour.Even a small chocolate wrapper they will throw in the dustbin," the high court said.The bench then questioned, "Is this the price of liberty and democracy?"The court also voiced concern over the large quantity of plastic waste strewn across public places, observing that even Mumbai's beaches are littered with plastic. It questioned whether such conditions reflected the standards of "a civilised society".The judges noted that garbage dumped on roads and in narrow lanes poses serious health and hygiene risks to residents every day.Referring to the Municipal Corporation of Greater Mumbai's slogan 'Swachch Mumbai, Sundar Mumbai, Aapli Mumbai, Sundar Mumbai', the court said the civic body's intention was commendable but was being undermined by irresponsible behaviour from citizens and inadequate enforcement by the municipal machinery."It is in these circumstances the role of MCGM's cleanliness machinery wardwise becomes significant, to take all effective steps so that public streets are not used by the citizens as dumping places," the bench observed.The court said failing to enforce the rules would defeat the objective behind the civic body's cleanliness campaign and urged authorities to implement the existing regulations strictly.It also raised concerns over the handling of garbage near heritage landmarks such as Rajabai Tower and the Bombay high court building. The bench observed that tourists, including foreign visitors, often encounter garbage on roads because of poor waste handling by municipal collection vehicles.The high court directed the civic body to take corrective steps within a week, warning that it would otherwise be compelled to pass further orders.
Article Summary: The court stressed that maintaining cleanliness is a fundamental duty and called for strict action against offenders. Justices G S Kulkarni and Aarti Sathe made the observations while hearing a batch of petitions over pollution, foul odour, gas emissions and health hazards linked to the Kanjurmarg dumping ground.

Suspected cases are isolated immediately and samples are tested at designated reference laboratories before a diagnosis is confirmed.

Article Title: After made-in-India bullet train, new high-speed corridors to get indigenous signalling system
Article Text:
India will develop its own control protocols for high-speed rail.

India’s indigenous signalling system for bullet trains

7 High-Speed Rail Corridors Planned

India is aiming to achieve new milestones in manufacturing with its first bullet train project. After deciding to manufacture the high-speed train indigenously for the Mumbai-Ahmedabad bullet train corridor, Indian Railways is now looking at in-house advanced signalling system for other upcoming corridors.Indian Railways is developing an indigenous signalling protocol for high-speed rail called the Bharat Train Control System (BTCS). The system is being designed specifically for Indian operating conditions and aims to eliminate dependence on foreign signalling protocols for the nearly 7,000 km of new bullet train corridors planned across the country.Earlier this month, former Japanese minister Hideki Makihara criticised India for not exclusively adopting Japanese technology for the MAHSR project, pointing to its decision to use open-source signalling protocols instead of Japan's Digital Automatic Train Control system.Responding to these concerns, officials said trains supplied by Japan's Hitachi are compatible with ETCS, but added that "offers from them (Japan) need to come first".Also Read | Why India making its own bullet trains is a big deal - explained The official further said India is also "open to allowing switchover to Japanese protocols once suppliers place appropriate proposals".Officials told ET that approvals for the designs and route alignments of future high-speed rail corridors are expected to be completed by mid-2027."India will develop its own control protocols for high-speed rail," a senior official told the financial daily, adding that the new system will build on the experience gained from the Mumbai-Ahmedabad High Speed Rail (MAHSR) corridor, where the European Train Control System (ETCS) is currently being deployed."The Bharat Train Control System will be open-source, cost-effective and can be tailored to requirements of rapid and safe deployment across the country," the official said, adding that once developed, the technology could also be offered to other countries.The official added that introducing an indigenous high-speed rail signalling protocol would provide a significant boost to domestic railway design companies and equipment manufacturers.In June last year, the National High Speed Rail Corporation Ltd (NHSRCL) awarded a Rs 4,100 crore contract for the signalling system on the Mumbai-Ahmedabad High Speed Rail (MAHSR) corridor to a consortium comprising India's Dineshchandra R Agrawal Infracon Pvt Ltd and Germany's Siemens.The consortium is deploying an ETCS Level 2-based signalling system capable of supporting train operations at speeds of up to 350 kmph.The Delhi-Meerut Rapid Rail Corridor, which currently operates India's fastest train, is also equipped with ETCS Level 2 signalling, supplied and implemented by France's Alstom.According to industry observers, the decision to adopt ETCS Level 2 for the Japan-backed MAHSR project enabled a broader pool of equipment suppliers to participate.
Article Summary: Indian Railways is developing an indigenous signalling protocol for high-speed rail. The Bharat Train Control System (BTCS) is being designed specifically for Indian operating conditions. The system aims to eliminate dependence on foreign signalling protocols for the nearly 7,000 km of new bullet train corridors.

Article Title: Tahir Hussain gets life for IB staffer’s killing in 2020 riots
Article Text:
'

Only death sentence will be justice’

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Bringing the six-year-long trial in the murder of Intelligence Bureau staffer Ankit Sharma to a close, a Delhi court on Friday sentenced former AAP councillor Tahir Hussain and four others to life imprisonment, holding that Sharma was lynched “solely on account of his religion” during the 2020 northeast Delhi riots.Additional sessions judge Parveen Kumar Singh, however, declined the prosecution’s plea for the death penalty, ruling that while the brutality of the crime was undeniable, the prosecution had failed to prove any specific act committed by each convict during the murder.Pronouncing the sentence, Singh described the murder as one of exceptional brutality committed during the “communal violence that erupted in the wake of the protests against CAA/NRC”.The court held that the prosecution failed to prove allegations that Hussain had “aided, abetted, instigated or led the unlawful assembly”. Singh rejected the other convicts’ pleas that they were sole breadwinners. However, he did consider their educational background as a mitigating factor.On July 13, the court had convicted Hussain and four others, holding that the five were part of “a large crowd which, with animus against Hindus, had assembled...with a common object to commit rioting, loot, arson and to cause damage to the property and person of members of the Hindu community”, before murdering the IB staffer on Feb 25, 2020, whose body was later recovered from a drain.Hussain was sentenced to six months’ RI under IPC Section 188, three years under Section 153A, two years under Section 147, three years under Section 148, seven years under Section 365 and imprisonment for life under Section 302. All sentences will run concurrently. He was also fined Rs 1,000 under Section 188, Rs 20,000 each under Sections 153A, 147 and 148, Rs 50,000 under Section 365 and Rs 5 lakh under Section 302, with default sentences in case of non-payment.“The manner in which it was committed was of the utmost brutality. The victim was sucked in by the murderous mob, baying for blood... The assault was so fierce, unrelenting, and from such close quarters that even in death, the body did not immediately slump to the ground,” the judge held.The court noted that the violence did not end with Sharma’s death. His body, it observed, was strapped “like an animal”, dragged to Chand Bagh pulia and thrown into a drain. Calling it an “aggravating circumstance of immense magnitude”, the judge remarked, “As if the hatred had still not been satiated, the dead body was thereafter thrown into the nala. Therefore, the barbarity with which this horrendous murder was committed is nauseatingly sickening. ”Saying the “crime test” tilted the case towards the “rarest of rare” category, the judge weighed aggravating and mitigating circumst-ances before declining the capital punishment sought by special public prosecutor Madhukar Pandey, who maintained that the offence was part of “well-orchestrated communal violence” rather than a crime committed und-er sudden provocation.The court zoomed in on what it found to be the prosecution’s principal shortcoming — the lack of specificity regarding the individual role of each convict. Observing that “before a life is ordered to be extinguished by a judicial decree”, something more than mere membership of an unlawful assembly had to be proved, the judge held that the prosecution had failed to bridge that gap. While acknowledging the state’s contention that the use of a heavy cutting weapon reflected pre-planned and cold-blooded intent, the court said the time for drawing such inferences was long past and treated the lack of specificity as a “huge mitigation. ”Judge Singh rejected the convicts’ pleas that they were sole breadwinners and noted that the “monstrosity of the crime committed outweighs this mitigating circumstance”. At the same time, he found no material to conclude that they were beyond reform.It also noted that allegations of Hussain’s house being used as a “launchpad” for the riots were neither part of the charges framed nor specifically proved during trial. The judge also took note of the “entirely satisfactory” custodial conduct of Hussain, Kasim and Nazim, barring minor infractions by Kasim.Another mitigating factor, the court said, was the educational background of the convicts. It observed that “vested interests” had spread misinformation and whipped up a “religious frenzy”, making the uneducated co-convicts “more gullible and susceptible to such propaganda”, and held that this vulnerability to manipulation was relevant while determining the sentence.Hussain’s co-convicts were awarded life imprisonment under Section 302 IPC with a fine of Rs 25,000 each. They were also sentenced to six months under Section 188, three years under Section 153A, two years under Section 147, three years under Section 148 and seven years under Section 365 IPC, along with fines ranging from Rs 1,000 to Rs 10,000 under the respective provisions. All the sentences will run concurrently.As Hussain was being led out of the courtroom by police after the sentencing, he turned to those present and said, “High court se insaaf milega. Der aaye, lekin durust aaye.”Speaking to TOI, Ankur Sharma, brother of the IB staffer, said, “From day one, this has been a ‘rarest of rare’ case. While we appreciate that the trial court has delivered a conviction and handed down life imprisonment, true justice won’t be served until the perpetrators receive the death sentence, a demand we will aggressively pursue in the high court. The sheer brutality of the crime still haunts our family every single day; knowing he was inflicted with 51 wounds, subjected to acid, and dumped in a drain is a pain that never truly goes away. ”
Article Summary: Former AAP councillor Tahir Hussain and four others sentenced to life imprisonment. Sharma was lynched “solely on account of his religion’ during 2020 northeast Delhi riots. Prosecution failed to prove allegations that Hussain had “aided, abetted, instigated or led the unlawful assembly.

Article Title: Monsoon likely to be ‘below normal’ in Aug-Sept: IMD
Article Text:
July rain gives hope to farm sector

NEW DELHI: Average rainfall in India during the second half of monsoon season (Aug-Sept) is most likely to be ‘below normal’, IMD said Friday, flagging the continuing risk of El Niño, which is associated with a weak monsoon.Last month, IMD had cited El Niño’s impact to forecast below normal rains in July. The month’s rainfall turned out to be normal due to plentiful showers in central India. The met department attributed this to “intra-seasonal variability”, saying a record 24 days were under the influence of ‘low pressure systems’ (LPS) in July against normal of about 13.5 days.“Four LPS were formed over Bay of Bengal that led to good rainfall from Odisha to Gujarat. We need to further analyse the reason (for better-than-expected July rains). These LPS couldn’t be captured by our long-range forecast model,” said Mrutyunjay Mohapatra, IMD chief.Two long wet spells, one during the first week of July and the second from July 22 onwards, helped reduce the overall monsoon rainfall deficit in the country from 35% in June to nearly 13% at the end of July. Since the ‘monsoon core zone’, where farming operations remain mainly rain-fed, largely coincides with central India, good rains in the region could aid recovery of acreage in the month.Though overall acreage of the summer sown crops continues to be in deficit compared to the corresponding period last year, the deficit reduced from nearly 21% on July 3 to around 3% on July 31, giving hope to the farm sector in an El Nino year.During Aug-Sept, IMD said certain parts of peninsular India, central India, northern parts of northwest India, and east and northeast India may get “normal to above-normal” rains, but it may not change the forecast of overall ‘below normal’ quantitative rainfall in the country.
Article Summary: Average rainfall in India during the second half of monsoon season is most likely to be ‘below normal’ IMD flagging the continuing risk of El Niño, which is associated with a weak monsoon. Last month, IMD had cited El Niño’s impact to forecast below normal rains in July.

Article Title: Ethanol kept petrol prices lower: Govt
Article Text: NEW DELHI: Petrol would have cost around Rs 125 a litre in the national capital when global crude prices touched $135 a barrel had oil companies not blended ethanol into the auto fuel, the petroleum ministry said on Friday, defending the programme against what it described as "misleading" claims about its costs, impact on food security and alleged taxpayer subsidy.It said consumers paid Rs 94.77 per litre because 20% of every litre comprised domestically produced ethanol procured at pre-agreed prices, helping shield retail fuel prices from the global crude price spike. "The result was nearly Rs 30 per litre in savings at the pump during the peak of the crisis," it noted.Govt kept petrol and diesel prices unchanged for nearly 75 days after West Asia conflict began on Feb 28 before raising them by Rs 7.5 per litre in May. The 91-octane standard E20 petrol now costs Rs 102.12 per litre in Delhi, while 100-octane petrol is priced at Rs 169 per litre.The ministry also rejected allegations that foodgrain meant for poor was being diverted for ethanol production or that subsidised FCI rice was being used to support the programme.
Article Summary: Petrol would have cost around Rs 125 a litre in the national capital when global crude prices touched $135 a barrel. 20% of every litre comprised domestically produced ethanol procured at pre-agreed prices. Govt kept petrol and diesel prices unchanged for nearly 75 days after West Asia conflict began.

Article Title: 16.4% deleted in Haryana draft roll; 10.8% in Andhra Pradesh
Article Text:

Andhra draft roll

drops 44.9L names

Nearly 16.4% of the electorate in Haryana and 10.8% in Andhra Pradesh were excluded in draft voter rolls published for the two states Friday as part of phase 3 of special intensive revision (SIR).In Haryana, the total strength of electors in the draft roll was 83.6% of 2.1 crore at the start of SIR on May 14. Of those deleted in the enumeration phase, 3.7% (7.7 lakh) have been marked by booth-level officers as dead; 11.7% (24.1 lakh) as permanently shifted, absent or untraceable; and 1% (2 lakh) as enrolled at more than one place.In all, 33.8 lakh names have been struck off the draft rolls, bringing the electorate down to 1.7 crore.Over 89.2% of 4.2 crore electors enrolled in Andhra Pradesh at the start of Special Intensive Revision submitted their enumeration forms, with the remaining 3.7% found deceased; 5.3% permanently shifted, absent or untraceable; and 1.8% enrolled at multiple places.The draft roll published Friday lists a total 3.7 crore electors in Andhra, after deletion of 44.9 lakh voters.AP chief electoral officer (CEO) Vivek Yadav and Haryana CEO A Srinivas attributed the non-collection of 10.6% and 16.4% enumeration forms, respectively, to the corresponding electors having enrolled in another state or UT, not being found by BLOs, not having submitted the form within the deadline (July 24), or simply not willing to register as an elector.Genuine electors can still be added back in the electoral rolls during the claims and objections period, which will run from July 31 to Aug 30, by filling up Form 6, along with the prescribed declaration form.
Article Summary: Nearly 16.4% of the electorate in Haryana and 10.8% in Andhra Pradesh were excluded in draft voter rolls published for the two states Friday. Of those deleted in the enumeration phase, 3.7% (7.7 lakh) have been marked by booth- level officers as dead.

Article Title: 2 years after death, Supreme Court clears former PM Manmohan Singh in Coalgate case
Article Text:
File photo: Former PM Manmohan Singh

NEW DELHI: More than 11 years after a Delhi court sensationally summoned former PM Manmohan Singh as an accused in a coal block allotment scam case, the Supreme Court Wednesday gave him a clean chit, closing the case nearly two years after his demise.Special judge Bharat Parashar, presiding over trials in coal block allotment scam cases which were investigated by the CBI under the SC’s monitoring, had on March 11, 2015, issued summons to Singh in the case relating to irregular allocation of Talabira-II coal block in Odisha to Kumar Mangalam Birla-owned Hindalco. Singh held the charge of coal ministry at the time of the allocation in question.Parashar, now the secretary general of SC, had declined to close the cases despite the CBI filing two successive reports — on Aug 27, 2014, and Oct 21, 2014 — recommending the same.Since the Supreme Court had barred Delhi HC from entertaining appeals against interim orders of the special judge, Singh moved SC challenging trial court’s order.A bench of Justices V Gopala Gowda and C Nagappan had on April 1, 2015, stayed the summoning order, saving the ex-PM the embarrassment of appearing as an accused in the Patiala House Court complex.On Wednesday, senior advocate Kapil Sibal, who had earlier successfully argued in SC for staying the proceedings against Singh, told a bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalaya Bagchi and V Mohana that though the proceedings would abate due to Singh’s demise in Nov 2024, the court should remove the trial court’s observations against the ex-PM in the summoning order.Senior advocate Abhishek Manu Singhvi joined Sibal to reiterate the request.Both the special public prosecutor and senior advocate R S Cheema and additional solicitor general S V Raju had recused themselves, leaving the court with the task of perusing the CBI closure reports on its own before passing the order.The CJI-led bench said the demise of an accused would ordinarily result in the abatement of case against him. After perusing the closure reports, it allowed Singh’s appeal and quashed the trial court’s order taking cognisance of the crime and issuing summons to Singh.
Article Summary: A Delhi court sensationally summoned former PM Manmohan Singh as an accused in a coal block allotment scam case. The Supreme Court Wednesday gave him a clean chit, closing the case nearly two years after his demise. Singh held the charge of coal ministry at the time of the allocation in question.

Article Title: Cabinet approved two major tunnel projects in J&K
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Cabinet Friday approved two strategic tunnel projects and the approach roads on NH-244 in J&K at an estimated cost of around Rs 9,800 crore to provide all-weather connectivity between Kashmir Valley and Jammu region while improving access to Chenab Valley.The projects comprise Singhpora-Vailoo tunnel and Sudhmahadev-Dranga tunnel, along with their approach roads, on the Anantnag-Chenani corridor. These are expected to strengthen road connectivity in Doda, Kishtwar and Udhampur districts, and reduce travel time.While the 39-km Singhapora-Vailoo stretch will have 10-km unidirectional twin-tube tunnels, the 13-km Sudhmahadev–Dranga section will have 8-km twin tube tunnels. The projects would be completed in five years and these will be fully Centre-funded.The tunnels are aimed at bypassing difficult stretches of NH-244 that are frequently affected by snowfall, landslides and adverse weather, disrupting traffic and isolating several areas during the winter months. Once completed, the projects will provide a safer and more efficient route for commuters, tourists and freight movement.Officials said the projects would boost regional connectivity by ensuring year-round access to remote districts, facilitating faster movement of essential goods and emergency services. Improved road infrastructure is also expected to promote tourism, trade and economic activity in the Chenab Valley, besides creating employment opportunities during the construction phase.The tunnel projects form part of the Centre’s broader strategy to modernise transport infrastructure in J&K and improve connectivity to border and hilly regions. Govt has undertaken several major road projects in the Union Territory, including the Chenani-Nashri Tunnel, the Zojila Tunnel and the Z-Morh Tunnel, to provide seamless and all-weather road links.
Article Summary: The projects comprise Singhpora-Vailoo tunnel and Sudhmahadev-Dranga tunnel. These are expected to strengthen road connectivity in Doda, Kishtwar and Udhampur districts. The projects would be completed in five years and these will be fully Centre-funded.

Article Title: India screens nearly 11,000 travellers after Ebola emergency, no case detected
Article Text:
Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: India has screened 10,974 international travellers arriving from Ebola-affected countries since May 23 after the World Health Organization declared the Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak a Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC), with no case detected in the country so far, the Centre informed Parliament on Friday.The government said surveillance and preparedness were intensified across the country following the WHO declaration, with enhanced screening at airports and other points of entry, mandatory travel declarations, designated isolation facilities, expanded laboratory capacity and nationwide mock drills to prepare for any suspected case.According to the ministry of health and family welfare, all international passengers are screened for recent travel to Democratic Republic of Congo, Uganda and South Sudan—countries affected by the Ebola outbreak. The government has not imposed a blanket travel ban, but passengers with travel history to these countries during the previous 21 days are identified through Self Declaration Forms, including the Air Suvidha 2.0 portal.Mumbai accounted for the highest number of screened passengers at 7,568, followed by Delhi (1,833), Hyderabad (532), Chennai (210), Bengaluru (205) and Ahmedabad (200). At the state level, Gujarat recorded the highest number of screened passengers (2,905), followed by Maharashtra (2,228), Uttar Pradesh (785), Tamil Nadu (731), Telangana (624) and Kerala (554).Replying to a question in the Lok Sabha, Union Health Minister J P Nadda said the Centre had coordinated its response with the National Centre for Disease Control (NCDC), Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR), Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS), Ministry of Civil Aviation and other agencies to strengthen surveillance and preparedness.The preparedness measures include issuing standard operating procedures covering surveillance, quarantine, laboratory testing, infection prevention and clinical management; identifying and operationalising isolation facilities across states and Union Territories; expanding diagnostic capacity through ICMR-NIV Pune and additional Biosafety Level-3 laboratories; deploying additional doctors and paramedical staff at major international airports; and conducting mock drills in designated hospitals nationwide.The government has also strengthened public awareness through airport displays, in-flight announcements, social media campaigns and a 24×7 national helpline while activating the NCDC Public Health Emergency Operations Centre to coordinate the response.The health ministry said no Ebola case has been reported in India so far.
Article Summary: India has screened 10,974 international travellers arriving from Ebola-affected countries since May 23. The government has not imposed a blanket travel ban, but passengers with travel history to these countries during the previous 21 days are identified. Mumbai accounted for the highest number of screened passengers at 7,568.

Article Title: Floating solar plants get Rs 5,000cr push
Article Text: Seeking to increase the Floating Solar Photovoltaic (FSPV) capacity to 5,000 mw from 700 mw, the Centre Friday cleared a Rs 5,070 crore scheme to push development of floating solar projects along with storage set-ups with a minimum capacity of 2 hours. These aim to utilise existing water reservoirs to set up solar plants, helping eliminating competition for land resources. National Institute of Solar Energy declared Maharashtra (16.3 gw) has the highest FSPV potential, which followed by Madhya Pradesh (14.9 gw), and Karnataka (13.7 gw). TNN
Article Summary: The Centre Friday cleared a Rs 5,070 crore scheme to push development of floating solar projects. These aim to utilise existing water reservoirs to set up solar plants. Maharashtra (16.3 gw) has the highest FSPV potential, followed by Madhya Pradesh (14.9 gw), and Karnataka (13.7 gw).

Article Title: Govt extends PM-Kisan yojana
Article Text: Govt Friday approved continuation of the farmers’ income support scheme, Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi (PM-Kisan) Yojana, from 2026-27 to 2030-31 with a total financial outlay of Rs 3.1 lakh crore. Under the scheme, eligible landholding farmer families get financial assistance of Rs 6,000 per year in three equal instalments of Rs 2,000 each. Govt said, “...This has enhanced farmers’ productive capacity...”
Article Summary: Govt Friday approved continuation of the farmers’ income support scheme, Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi. Under the scheme, eligible landholding farmer families get financial assistance of Rs 6,000 per year in three equal instalments of Rs 2,000 each.

Article Title: Samudra Manthan gets Cabinet nod
Article Text: Union Cabinet approved Samudra Manthan Friday, a Rs 84,084-crore national offshore exploration programme to step up oil and gas exploration in India’s offshore basins to reduce dependence on imports, reports Atul Mathur. The scheme aims to increase exploration in deepwater and ultra-deepwater areas through large-scale seismic surveys, exploratory drilling and creation of common offshore infrastructure in the next five years.
Article Summary: The scheme aims to increase exploration in deepwater and ultra-deepwater areas through large-scale seismic surveys, exploratory drilling and creation of common offshore infrastructure in the next five years. Union Cabinet approved Samudra Manthan Friday, a Rs 84,084-crore national offshore exploration programme.

Article Title: SC slaps Rs 1 lakh fine on Rajasthan government for harassing official
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Frowning upon "interference" by the joint secretary of the then chief minister of Rajasthan in May 2018 in a matter of granting sanction to prosecute a govt official, Supreme Court has directed the state to pay 1 lakh to the official for harassing him.A bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran said the provision of sanction was meant to safeguard innocent public servants from frivolous harassment."The decision-making process under Section 19 of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988, cannot resemble the dilemma in Hamlet's Soliloquy: 'to be or not to be', though expressed in a different context. If there is ambivalence, it could be presumed that extraneous considerations weighed and here is a case where political dictate is blatantly displayed," the bench said.The bench took a serious view of the blatant display of "political dictate" by the state in dragging a public servant to court."We cannot but observe that the petitioner has been dragged unnecessarily to the high court by the review, prompted by the office of the CM. The state at least should have rested content, when the highest constitutional court within its boundaries interfered with a patently illegal and blatantly tainted order of sanction.We hence dismiss the special leave petition with the above observations and further direction to the state to pay cost quantified at 50,000 each before high court and this court," the bench said."The deliberate digression from essential duties, presumably on political considerations, commenced when the joint secretary of the chief minister on 24.05.2018 referred back the matter for reconsideration, asserting that the money recovered from the table drawer of the petitioner clearly proved the acceptance of bribe," it said.
Article Summary: Justices J B Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran said the provision of sanction was meant to safeguard innocent public servants from frivolous harassment. The bench took a serious view of the blatant display of "political dictate" by the state in dragging a public servant to court.

Article Text: NEW DELHI: Congratulating UK PM Andy Burnham on assuming office, PM Narendra Modi said the two leaders will collaborate closely to fully harness the trade and investment opportunities presented by the recently operationalised India-UK Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA), for the "shared prosperity and well-being of both our people".Burnham officially took office as UK PM on July 20, 2026.The leaders discussed the West Asia conflict, agreeing to continue to work closely together towards de-escalation and the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz. Article Title: Cabinet eases captive waterfront norms to spur private investment
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Cabinet Friday approved a revision to the shipping ministry’s captive waterfront policy to accelerate private investment by providing greater operational certainty and allowing govt entities to obtain waterfronts on a nomination basis.The revised Policy for Award of Waterfront and Associated Land to Port-Dependent Industries (Captive Policy) introduces a series of reforms aimed at improving operational flexibility and strengthening infrastructure development at major ports.The shipping ministry said the revised policy allows existing captive users to develop additional berths, jetties, terminals and Single Buoy Moorings (SBMs) to meet enhanced captive requirements. It also extends the concession period to up to 30 years for govt entities while addressing changes arising from evolving business needs and regulatory conditions.Officials said there were around 24 captive waterfront facilities as of last year.“The policy is expected to provide greater certainty to investors, facilitate capacity augmentation and improve the ease of doing business in the port sector without any financial implication for the government,” the ministry said.The revised policy also provides a framework for allotting waterfronts and associated land to eligible government organisations on a nomination basis, without resorting to competitive bidding, subject to availability and prescribed safeguards.Eligible entities include Central and state govt departments, statutory authorities, autonomous bodies, public sector undertakings (PSUs) and government-controlled joint ventures operating in sectors such as fertilisers, food, petroleum, oil and gas, coal, and steel, as notified by the shipping ministry.Under the revised policy, concessions will be awarded at the notified floor price.
Article Summary: Cabinet Friday approved a revision to the shipping ministry’s captive waterfront policy. Reforms aimed at improving operational flexibility and strengthening infrastructure development at major ports. It also extends the concession period to up to 30 years for govt entities.

Article Title: J&K: Properties of 11 Pak-based terrorist handlers attached in Ramban
Article Text:

JAMMU: J&K Police attached properties of 11 Pakistan-based terrorist handlers in Ramban district on Friday to prevent their misuse for terror financing in the Union Territory.The assets belonged to terrorist handlers Mohammed Iqbal, Farooq Ahmed, Bashir Ahmed, Atta Mohd Khanday, Mohd Yaseen, Tariq Hussain, Mohd Rafiq, Muzzafer, Abdul Qadir Naik, Mohd Iqbal Wani, and Abdul Waheed. They were currently operating as terrorist handlers from across the border, actively promoting, facilitating, and coordinating activities of ultras. The accused had allegedly planned to use the assets to facilitate, finance, and sustain terror acts,” the spokesperson said.The action was part of J&K Police’s ongoing efforts to dismantle the financial and logistical infrastructure of cross-border terror networks. In a similar exercise Thursday (July 30), police attached properties of five Pakistan-based terrorist handlers in Reasi district. In yet another such operation on Wednesday (July 29), cops attached assets worth over Rs 90 lakh in Ramban district, belonging to four terrorist handlers operating from Pakistan and Pakistan-occupied Kashmir.

Article Title: Assam floods: Death toll rises to 80; state shifts focus to rehabilitation, announces loan relief
Article Text:
Rescue teams continue relief operations

Government announces loan relief package

Cloudburst triggered unprecedented flooding: CM

Two more deaths in Sivasagar pushed Assam's flood toll to 80 on Friday, even as more than 2.12 lakh people across eight districts continued to grapple with the deluge.The latest figures mark an improvement from the previous day's situation, when the flood toll stood at 78, over 3 lakh people across seven districts were affected, and floodwaters had inundated 551 villages and more than 21,500 hectares of crop area.21 revenue circles and 437 villages remain inundated across Golaghat, Sivasagar, Biswanath, Charaideo, Kamrup (Metropolitan), Jorhat, Dhemaji and Nagaon. Charaideo remains the worst-hit district with nearly 80,000 affected people, followed by Sivasagar (71,000) and Jorhat (40,000), PTI cites.Floodwaters have also caused extensive damage to embankments, roads, bridges and other public infrastructure.According to the recent data shared by the government, relief operations are continuing across Assam, with 216 relief camps and 1,788 relief distribution centres supporting flood-affected communities. The camps are currently sheltering 71,416 people, while authorities continue to provide food, drinking water, medicines and other essential supplies. Sarma said rehabilitation efforts remain the government's top priority as floodwaters recede.The Army, NDRF, SDRF, Fire and Emergency Services, police and civil administration remain engaged in rescue and relief efforts.In an X post, CM Himanta wrote, "Our teams are working 24*7 while we are formulating policies to directly benefit the affected."With floodwaters receding, Sarma said the administration has expanded relief work to include debris clearance, doorstep healthcare, disposal of animal carcasses, disinfection drives, restoration of electricity and other essential services.Chief minister Himanta Biswa Sarma on Thursday also announced a six-month moratorium on repayment of loans availed by flood-affected people in Sivasagar, Charaideo, Jorhat and Golaghat districts. The decision was taken at a special meeting of the State Level Bankers' Committee (SLBC), attended by representatives of the RBI, NABARD, SBI and other commercial banks.Banks have also agreed to extend loan tenures by one to seven years, depending on the type of loan, he informed. The Assam government has sought a special relief package from the Centre and urged the Inter-Ministerial Central Team (IMCT) to classify the Upper Assam floods as an "atypical, high-intensity, rapid-onset event" for more flexible relief norms.Meanwhile, Assam ministers flagged off 30 trucks carrying food, clothing and other essential supplies for flood-hit districts.Assam minister Atul Bora, talking to ANI, said the government was continuing relief operations on a war footing and highlighted the Rs 15,000 financial assistance announced for each affected family, in addition to food supplies and other necessities.Earlier, chief minister Himanta Biswa Sarma had attributed the devastating floods to an intense cloudburst in the upstream states of Arunachal Pradesh and Nagaland.In a post on X on July 22, he said Arunachal Pradesh received 141% above-normal rainfall, while Nagaland recorded 181% above-normal precipitation, resulting in an unprecedented discharge of floodwaters into Assam.Sarma said the sudden surge inundated several districts that had witnessed little or no flooding in recent history.
Article Summary: Two more deaths in Sivasagar pushed Assam's flood toll to 80 on Friday. More than 2.12 lakh people across eight districts continue to grapple with the deluge. Charaideo remains the worst-hit district with nearly 80,000 affected people.

Article Title: Explained: India's first urban ropeway is almost here. Can Varanasi's sky-high commute change how Indian cities travel?
Article Text:
Varanasi Urban Ropeway is India's first ropeway designed primarily as an urban mass transit system rather than a tourist attraction

What exactly is the Varanasi Urban Ropeway?

Why is the government betting on ropeways?

Can ropeways really work as urban public transport?

Could Varanasi become a model for other Indian cities?

The bigger picture

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

For centuries, getting around Varanasi has been part of the city's experience.Its narrow lanes, bustling bazaars, temples and ghats are integral to the spiritual capital's identity. But as one of India's oldest continuously inhabited cities welcomed millions of pilgrims and tourists every year, those same streets also became one of its biggest infrastructure challenges.The stretch between Varanasi Cantonment railway station and Godowlia, the gateway to the Kashi Vishwanath Temple and Dashashwamedh Ghat, often witnessed bumper-to-bumper traffic.During festivals or the peak pilgrimage season, a journey of less than four kilometres could easily take 40 minutes or more.Building wider roads was never a practical solution. Much of the corridor passes through densely populated neighbourhoods and heritage areas, where large-scale demolition would not only be expensive but also risk altering the city's centuries-old character.Instead, policymakers looked upwards.Later this year, Varanasi is expected to become home to India's first urban public transport ropeway—a project that promises to ferry commuters and pilgrims above the city's congested streets in gondola cabins suspended nearly 45-50 metres above the ground.Unlike the ropeways familiar to tourists in hill stations, this one is being built as part of the city's everyday mass transit network.Officials say it will cut travel time between Cantt and Godowlia from around 40-45 minutes by road to roughly 15 minutes, while reducing pressure on one of the city's busiest traffic corridors.The project is also a global rarity. Urban ropeways are still uncommon worldwide, with only a handful of cities integrating them into their public transport networks. Indian officials have frequently described the Varanasi project as among the first of its kind globally to use ropeway technology for mass urban commuting rather than tourism.Beyond offering a faster ride for pilgrims heading to the Kashi Vishwanath Temple, the project is being viewed as a test case for whether aerial mobility can solve transport problems in India's densely populated and heritage-rich cities, where conventional infrastructure often faces severe space constraints.If successful, it could influence similar projects planned in cities ranging from Guwahati and Shimla to Dehradun and beyond under the Centre's broader ropeway expansion programme.That makes Varanasi more than just another infrastructure project, as it could become the template for a new model of urban transport in India.So, what exactly is India's first urban ropeway? Why has the government chosen cable cars over roads or metro lines? And can this technology genuinely become part of India's future public transport network?The Varanasi Urban Ropeway is India's first ropeway designed primarily as an urban mass transit system rather than a tourist attraction.The project is being implemented by the National Highways Logistics Management Limited (NHLML), a wholly owned company of the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI), under the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways. Swiss ropeway manufacturer Bartholet Maschinenbau AG has supplied the cable transport technology for the project.Once operational, the ropeway will connect Varanasi Cantonment railway station with Godowlia Chowk, one of the busiest intersections in the city and the main access point for pilgrims visiting the Kashi Vishwanath Temple.Stretching approximately 3.75-3.85 kilometres, the corridor will include stations at Cantt, Vidyapeeth, Rath Yatra and Godowlia, linking the railway station with major commercial, residential and religious hubs.The project was conceived after authorities concluded that expanding roads through Varanasi's congested core would be extremely difficult because of the city's dense urban fabric and heritage structures.Instead of competing for road space, the ropeway will operate entirely above existing traffic, offering commuters a predictable travel time regardless of congestion below.According to the government, the system will use 148 modern gondola cabins, each capable of carrying 10 passengers. Gondolas are expected to arrive every one-and-a-half to two minutes, allowing the system to transport nearly 3,000 passengers per hour in each direction, or about 6,000 passengers every hour in total.Official estimates suggest the network could eventually handle close to 96,000-1 lakh passengers daily, depending on operational schedules and demand.Passengers boarding at Cantt Railway Station will be able to reach Godowlia in about 15-16 minutes, less than half the time the journey often takes by road during busy hours.The Uttar Pradesh government has also finalised passenger fares. The minimum ticket has been fixed at Rs 10, while travelling the entire stretch from Cantt to Godowlia will cost Rs 50. Holders of the Kashi Smart Pass will receive a 20% discount, reducing the end-to-end fare to Rs 40. Premium gondolas have also been planned for tourists and group bookings.Modern passenger facilities, including lifts, escalators, CCTV surveillance, digital ticketing, fire safety systems and dedicated infrastructure for senior citizens and persons with disabilities, have been incorporated at stations to position the ropeway as a full-fledged public transport system rather than simply another tourist attraction.The project, estimated to cost over Rs 800 crore including long-term operation and maintenance, has already completed trial runs and is expected to begin commercial operations after receiving the necessary regulatory clearances.The Varanasi project is not an isolated experiment. It is part of the Centre's much larger strategy to introduce ropeways as an alternative mode of transport in places where building conventional roads, metro lines or rail corridors is either too expensive, technically difficult or environmentally disruptive.This vision took shape in 2022 with the launch of the Parvatmala Pariyojana, the National Ropeways Development Programme announced in the Union Budget. The scheme aims to develop ropeways in hilly regions as well as congested urban areas through public-private partnerships.Traditionally, ropeways in India have been associated with tourist destinations such as Gulmarg, Auli, Mussoorie or pilgrimage centres. Under the new policy, however, the government wants them to become part of mainstream public transport.Officials argue that ropeways offer several advantages over conventional infrastructure. They require significantly less land acquisition than roads or metro systems because towers occupy relatively small footprints.Construction is also faster since there is little need for tunnelling, large flyovers or extensive utility shifting. Since the cabins are electrically operated, ropeways also produce lower emissions than conventional road traffic, making them an attractive option for cities trying to reduce congestion and pollution.The Varanasi project perfectly fits this philosophy.The city's historic core leaves almost no room for widening roads without affecting heritage structures and densely populated neighbourhoods. A metro line would have involved far greater costs and engineering challenges.An aerial ropeway, planners argue, offers a way to increase mobility while preserving the city's cultural fabric.Prime Minister Narendra Modi had also highlighted this balance between tradition and technology when the project was announced.Sharing details of the ropeway on social media in 2023, he described it as an "adbhut sangam" (remarkable confluence) of faith and technology and said it would not only make travel more convenient for devotees but also improve access to the Kashi Vishwanath Temple.The government now sees ropeways as a solution that can complement—not replace—existing transport systems.The idea may appear futuristic in India, but urban ropeways have been operating successfully in several parts of the world for years.Perhaps the best-known example is La Paz, Bolivia, where the Mi Teleférico network has evolved into one of the world's largest urban cable car systems. With multiple interconnected lines stretching across the city and neighbouring El Alto, it carries hundreds of thousands of passengers every day while navigating mountainous terrain that makes conventional transport difficult.Another frequently cited example is Mexico City, whose Cablebús system has transformed commuting for residents living in densely populated hillside settlements.What once took well over an hour by road can now be completed in a fraction of the time using aerial cabins integrated with the city's wider public transport network.These examples have demonstrated that ropeways need not remain tourist attractions. They can function as reliable mass transit systems when integrated with buses, railways and pedestrian infrastructure.Varanasi is now attempting to replicate those successesUnlike metro systems that require passengers to travel underground or elevated through fixed corridors, ropeways can fly directly over existing development, reducing construction challenges and avoiding traffic altogether.Continuous movement of gondolas also means passengers spend less time waiting compared to conventional bus services.However, experts caution that ropeways are not a universal solution.Their passenger capacity is considerably lower than metro rail systems, making them suitable only for specific corridors rather than citywide transport. Weather conditions, periodic maintenance and evacuation protocols also require careful planning. Unlike buses, expanding routes later is neither simple nor inexpensive.Consequently, transport planners view ropeways as a niche solution—best suited for heritage cities, mountainous terrain or highly congested corridors where traditional transport networks are difficult to expand.That is perhaps the biggest question surrounding the project.If the ropeway succeeds in reducing congestion, attracting regular commuters and integrating smoothly with the city's existing transport network, it could become a blueprint for similar projects elsewhere.The Centre has already identified several ropeway proposals across the country under the Parvatmala programme, particularly in Himalayan states and pilgrimage destinations. Cities facing severe geographical or heritage constraints are also studying whether aerial mobility could complement existing infrastructure.But the success of the Varanasi ropeway will ultimately depend on far more than engineering.Passengers must find it affordable enough to use regularly. The stations need seamless connections with railway stations, buses, auto-rickshaws and pedestrian routes. Safety standards, maintenance schedules and operational reliability will determine whether commuters choose the ropeway over conventional road transport.Ridership will also be critical.Unlike tourist ropeways that witness seasonal demand, an urban transport system must attract consistent daily commuters—office-goers, students, residents and pilgrims—to remain financially viable over the long term.There is also the question of whether ropeways can genuinely ease congestion or merely shift it from roads to stations if passenger management is inadequate.These are precisely the issues transport planners and policymakers across India will be watching once commercial operations begin.India's urban transport story has traditionally revolved around roads, flyovers, suburban railways and metro systems. Ropeways are rarely featured in discussions about everyday commuting.Varanasi could change that.By carrying passengers above one of the country's oldest and most congested cities, the project represents an attempt to rethink how mobility solutions are designed for places where conventional infrastructure has reached its limits.Its significance therefore extends beyond the four-kilometre journey between Cantt and Godowlia.If successful, it could demonstrate that innovative transport systems can coexist with heritage conservation, allowing cities to modernise without fundamentally altering their historic character.At the same time, the project is also a reminder that no single technology can solve every urban mobility challenge. Ropeways are unlikely to replace metros or buses in India's largest cities. Instead, they could become another tool in the transport planner's toolkit—one best deployed where geography, density or heritage leave few alternatives.For Varanasi, the benefits could be immediate. Faster journeys for pilgrims, easier access to one of India's holiest temples, reduced traffic on chronically congested roads and a cleaner mode of transport for residents and visitors alike.For India, however, the stakes are much larger.The country's first urban public transport ropeway is not merely about moving people from one station to another.It is a test of whether the next generation of urban infrastructure can think beyond roads and rails and whether its oldest cities can embrace modern mobility without sacrificing the heritage that defines them.
Article Summary: The Varanasi Urban Ropeway is India's first ropeway designed primarily as an urban mass transit system rather than a tourist attraction. It promises to ferry commuters and pilgrims above the city's congested streets in gondola cabins suspended nearly 45-50 metres above the ground.

Article Title: IMD flags below-normal rainfall in August; heavy rain alerts for Kerala, Assam, Northeast
Article Text:
IMD predicts 94% rainfall across India for August

August outlook raises concerns for crops and economy

Kerala under orange alert, schools shut in several districts

Flash flood warning issued for Arunachal Pradesh

Assam and northeast brace for another spell of heavy rain

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The India Meteorological Department (IMD) on Friday forecast below-normal rainfall in August across India, at 94 per cent of the long-period average. It also issued weather alerts across several parts of the country, including Kerala, Assam, Arunachal Pradesh and other northeastern states, warning of heavy to very heavy rainfall, thunderstorms, flash floods and landslides over the next few days.The latest warnings come as several states continue to grapple with flood and landslide risks during the monsoon season. The IMD said monthly average rainfall over India as a whole is most likely to be below normal in August after the country recorded near-average rainfall in July, raising concerns about crop yields and broader economic activity."Rainfall in August is likely to be below 94% of the long-period average," Mrutyunjay Mohapatra, director-general of the India Meteorological Department, told a press conference.The IMD’s latest forecast of below-normal August rainfall comes after a season marked by intense regional downpours despite broadly average rainfall across the country in July. The weather office’s assessment suggests that while parts of southern and northeastern India may continue to experience heavy rain in the immediate term, rainfall across India as a whole is expected to remain below the long-term average during August.In Kerala, the IMD issued an orange alert for 11 districts on Friday, including Thiruvananthapuram, Kollam, Pathanamthitta, Alappuzha, Kottayam, Idukki, Ernakulam, Kozhikode, Wayanad, Kannur and Kasaragod. An orange alert indicates the likelihood of very heavy rainfall ranging between 115.6 mm and 204.4 mm within 24 hours at isolated places.For August 1, orange alerts remain in place for Idukki, Ernakulam, Thrissur, Palakkad, Malappuram, Kozhikode, Wayanad, Kannur and Kasaragod, while yellow alerts have been issued for several southern districts through August 2.Following the warnings, educational institutions in several Kerala districts were declared closed on Friday. The Kerala State Disaster Management Authority advised residents in areas vulnerable to landslides, mudslides and flash floods to move to safer locations if directed by authorities. People living near riverbanks, downstream of dams and in houses with weak roofs were also urged to remain vigilant.In Arunachal Pradesh, the IMD forecast heavy to very heavy rainfall accompanied by thunderstorms and lightning from July 31 and issued a flash flood alert for nine districts, including Tawang, West Kameng, East Kameng, Kurung Kumey, Upper Subansiri, Anjaw, Dibang Valley, Tirap and Changlang.Very heavy rainfall of 12 cm to 20 cm in 24 hours is expected at isolated places in Papum Pare district through Saturday, while Lower Subansiri is likely to receive heavy rainfall of 6 cm to 11 cm. The weather office warned that heavy rain could trigger surface runoff and inundation in saturated and low-lying areas and advised district administrations to remain on high alert.The ongoing spell of floods and landslides has already claimed seven lives and affected 1,53,553 people across Arunachal Pradesh. The monsoon has affected 373 circles and 668 villages in 27 districts so far.A fresh spell of heavy to very heavy rainfall has also been forecast across Assam and several northeastern states over the next three to four days. An orange alert has been issued for Tinsukia district in Assam, while similar alerts are in place for Mon, Mokokchung and Wokha districts of Nagaland.The IMD said widespread rainfall accompanied by thunderstorms is likely between July 30 and August 1 across parts of Assam, Arunachal Pradesh and Nagaland. Runoff from districts in Arunachal Pradesh, including East Siang, Lohit, Namsai, Longding, Papumpare, Lower Subansiri and Lower Dibang Valley, could affect Tinsukia, Dhemaji and Lakhimpur districts in Assam.The Assam State Disaster Management Authority warned that the fresh spell of rain could worsen flooding, trigger urban waterlogging and flash floods, and cause localised landslides, particularly in hilly and vulnerable areas. District administrations have been instructed to closely monitor the situation and residents have been urged to avoid non-essential travel during periods of intense rainfall.
Article Summary: IMD predicts 94% rainfall across India for August. August outlook raises concerns for crops and economy. schools shut in several districts in Kerala.Flash flood warning issued for Arunachal Pradesh. Assam and northeast brace for another spell of heavy rain.

Article Title: PM Modi, UK PM Andy Burnham discuss AI, defence, Strait of Hormuz in first phone call
Article Text:
UK highlights AI cooperation and vision 2035

Leaders discuss AI and emerging technologies

Middle East and Strait of Hormuz discussed

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Friday held his first telephone conversation with newly elected UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham, congratulating him on assuming office as the two leaders agreed to deepen cooperation in technology, artificial intelligence, defence, trade and security while also discussing the situation in the Middle East, including efforts to reopen the Strait of Hormuz.In a post on X after the call, PM Modi said he congratulated Burnham on taking office and reaffirmed India's commitment to strengthening the bilateral partnership."Delighted to speak with Prime Minister of the United Kingdom Andy Burnham. Congratulated him on assuming office and conveyed my best wishes for a successful tenure."The Prime Minister said both leaders agreed to expand cooperation across multiple strategic sectors."We agreed to work together across sectors such as technology, innovation, defence, security, clean energy, education and people-to-people ties and take the India-UK Comprehensive Strategic Partnership to new heights."PM Modi also said both countries would seek to maximise the benefits of the recently operationalised India-UK Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement."We will also collaborate closely to fully harness the trade and investment opportunities presented by the recently operationalized India-UK Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement, for the shared prosperity and well-being of both our people."According to a statement issued by the UK Prime Minister's Office, Burnham described the India-UK relationship as a strong partnership that had made a significant contribution to communities across Britain.The statement said Burnham outlined his ambition to further strengthen bilateral ties through the UK-India Vision 2035 framework and stronger people-to-people connections.The UK Prime Minister also praised the contribution of the Indian community to British society, while PM Modi referred to the historical connection between Manchester and Ahmedabad, describing the Gujarat city as the "Manchester of India".The UK Prime Minister's Office said Burnham reaffirmed his commitment to advancing the UK-India Technology Security Initiative, with both leaders identifying artificial intelligence and other cutting-edge technologies as key areas for future collaboration.The leaders also welcomed the opportunities created by the recently introduced India-UK Free Trade Agreement, saying it would generate economic benefits and create opportunities for people in both countries.Beyond bilateral ties, the two leaders discussed the evolving situation in the Middle East and agreed to work closely towards de-escalation.According to Downing Street, both sides also agreed to cooperate in efforts aimed at reopening the Strait of Hormuz, a strategically vital maritime route for global energy supplies and international trade.The UK Prime Minister's Office said both leaders agreed to remain in close contact and looked forward to speaking again soon and meeting in person at the earliest opportunity.
Article Summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi held his first telephone conversation with newly elected UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham. The two leaders agreed to deepen cooperation in technology, artificial intelligence, defence, trade and security. They also discussed the situation in the Middle East, including efforts to reopen the Strait of Hormuz.

Article Title: CM Dhami inaugurates Kalash Bandhan Maha rally in Bhagwanpur on 650th birth anniversary of Sant Guru Ravidas
Article Text:
CM Dhami inaugurates Kalash Bandhan Maha rally in Bhagwanpur on 650th birth anniversary of Sant Guru Ravidas

Uttarakhand Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami inaugurated the Kalash Bandhan Maha Rally organised at Chudiyala, Bhagwanpur, on the occasion of the 650th birth anniversary of Sant ShiromGuru Ravidas Ji.The Chief Minister offered prayers at the Sant Shiromani Guru Ravidas Temple before flagging off the Kalash Yatra. He later carried the ceremonial Kalash on his head and proceeded to the event venue at CMD Inter College.Addressing the gathering, Chief Minister Dhami said that in Indian culture, the Kalash symbolises auspiciousness, new beginnings, and prosperity. He described the campaign as a major initiative to spread Sant Guru Ravidas Ji's message of social harmony, equality, and humanity among the people.The Chief Minister said that Sant Guru Ravidas propagated the ideals of love, equality, and humanity during a time of deep social discrimination. He emphasised that a person's greatness is determined not by birth but by noble deeds and service to humanity. He added that a strong and harmonious nation cannot be built until discrimination is eliminated from society.Dhami said that under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi , the Centre and the Uttarakhand government are working on the principle of "Sabka Saath, Sabka Vikas, Sabka Vishwas, Sabka Prayas."He highlighted that welfare schemes such as the Ujjwala Yojana, Swachh Bharat Mission, Jal Jeevan Mission, Ayushman Bharat, and the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana have ensured that essential services reach poor, Dalit, underprivileged, and needy families. He said these initiatives are important steps towards realising Sant Guru Ravidas Ji's vision of an inclusive and harmonious society.Highlighting development works in the Bhagwanpur region, the Chief Minister said that flood protection works worth nearly Rs 12 crore have been completed in the Bahadurpur-Sonali area, a lake has been beautified at a cost of around Rs 3 crore, a modern school has been constructed for Rs 49 crore, a Block Public Health Unit has been established at the Community Health Centre, and a new tehsil building has been constructed for Rs 8 crore. He added that several other infrastructure projects, including roads, link roads, CC roads, and high-mast lighting, have also been completed in the region.The Chief Minister urged people to adopt Sant Guru Ravidas Ji's ideals of harmony, equality, and humanity in their lives and to pledge themselves to building a discrimination-free society through social harmony and public participation.Speaking on the occasion, Cabinet Minister Khajan Das said that Prime Minister Narendra Modi understood the importance of taking the teachings and ideals of great saints to every corner of the country. He said that the sacred soil from Sant Guru Ravidas Ji's birthplace at Govardhanpur in Kashi is being carried across the country through Kalash Yatras.He said that such an initiative has become possible under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi. He further stated that under the leadership of Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami, the Samrasta Sankalp Yatra is being launched in Uttarakhand to spread Sant Guru Ravidas Ji's message of social harmony, equality, and humanity to every section of society.Swami Nirmaldas Ji also addressed the gathering and praised Chief Minister Dhami for his continuous efforts towards the development of Uttarakhand. He said that every individual should follow the path shown by God, as those who deviate from it must eventually face the consequences of their actions.On the occasion, Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami presented ceremonial Kalashs to BJP district presidents from across Uttarakhand to launch the Kalash Bandhan Yatra in all districts of the state.
Article Summary: Uttarakhand Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami inaugurated the Kalash Bandhan Maha Rally organised at Chudiyala, Bhagwanpur, on the occasion of the 650th birth anniversary of Sant Shiromani Guru Ravidas Ji. He described the campaign as a major initiative to spread the message of social harmony, equality, and humanity.

Article Title: Govt summons Meta's global team over PM Modi post restriction, to question algorithmic bias
Article Text:
Government to seek answers on algorithmic bias

Meta apologised, government found explanation inadequate

Parliamentary panel to examine issue

Hyderabad Police also register cases

NEW DELHI: The Centre has summoned Meta's global team to explain the temporary restriction of Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Facebook post, with government officials set to question the social media giant on alleged algorithmic bias, the functioning of its content moderation systems and its role in maintaining public order, PTI reported citing sources.According to the sources, Meta's global team is expected to arrive in India sometime in the middle of next week. Besides appearing before government officials, the executives will also depose before a parliamentary panel.The move comes days after the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) summoned a senior Meta executive following the temporary restriction of Prime Minister Modi 's Facebook post addressing India's youth and promising stringent action against paper leaks.Sources told PTI that the government's interaction with Meta's global team would focus on whether the platform's algorithms exhibit bias, how those algorithms function and the company's broader responsibility in matters affecting public order.The officials are expected to "categorically" seek clarification on issues surrounding algorithmic bias and the manner in which Meta's content moderation systems operate, the sources said.Meta had earlier attributed the restriction of the Prime Minister's post to a technical glitch and issued an apology. However, according to PTI, MeitY considered the company's explanation "inadequate".Following the incident, Meta informed the ministry that content posted by Prime Minister Modi and certain other prominent accounts would be subjected to additional oversight on its platforms.The company also wrote to the government outlining enhanced safeguards, including multiple levels of review involving senior company officials before action is taken on posts published by the Prime Minister and other high-profile accounts.Apart from appearing before government officials, Meta's global representatives are also expected to testify before a parliamentary panel as scrutiny over the company's content moderation practices intensifies.Government sources told PTI that when platform rules or Indian laws are violated, liabilities would arise.The sources also pointed to studies highlighting the wider impact of social media on society, including concerns over cognitive health and mental well-being among both children and adults due to excessive digital media consumption."Keeping all these aspects in mind, steps that are needed will be taken," a government source told PTI, adding that the government was treating the matter seriously.The government's scrutiny comes amid parallel legal action in Telangana.Earlier this week, Hyderabad Cyber Crime Police registered cases against Meta India head Arun Srinivas and operators of several Facebook and Instagram accounts over allegedly morphed and AI-generated content targeting Prime Minister Modi during protests over the NEET paper leak issue.According to police, the cases were filed following complaints by BJP supporters alleging that manipulated videos and images of the Prime Minister were circulated on social media. Investigators have issued notices to Meta and are tracing the operators behind the accounts named in the complaints.The latest developments mark an escalation in the government's scrutiny of Meta, with the company now facing regulatory, parliamentary and law enforcement action over its content moderation practices and handling of politically sensitive content.
Article Summary: The Centre has summoned Meta's global team to explain the temporary restriction of Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Facebook post. Government officials are set to question the social media giant on alleged algorithmic bias, the functioning of its content moderation systems and its role in maintaining public order. Besides appearing before government officials, the executives will also depose before a parliamentary panel.

Article Title: Ethanol blending saved consumers Rs 30/litre during crude spike: Govt
Article Text:
Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Petrol was projected to cost around Rs 125 per litre in Delhi when global crude prices touched $135 a barrel if India had not blended ethanol with petrol, the petroleum ministry said on Friday, defending the ethanol-blending programme against what it described as “misleading” claims about its costs, impact on food security and alleged taxpayer subsidy.The clarification came amid criticism that Food Corporation of India (FCI) rice was supplied to distilleries at concessional rates, allegedly causing losses to the exchequer, and that ethanol blending survives only because ethanol is more expensive than petrol.The ministry said consumers paid Rs 94.77 per litre because 20% of every litre comprised domestically produced ethanol procured at pre-agreed prices, insulating retail fuel prices from the global crude price spike. “The result was nearly Rs 30 per litre in savings at the pump during the peak of the crisis,” it said.In a detailed clarification, the ministry rejected allegations that foodgrain meant for the poor was being diverted to produce ethanol or that subsidised rice supplied by the FCI was being used to artificially support the programme. “Ethanol is not built around cheap rice. It is built around a flexible mix of approved feedstocks, with FCI rice used only when certified surplus stocks are available after meeting every food security obligation,” the ministry said, adding that food security obligations always take precedence and that grain is released for ethanol production only after requirements under the public distribution system, National Food Security Act, welfare schemes and mandatory buffer stocks have been fully met.Responding to criticism over the supply of FCI rice to distilleries, the ministry said rice was only one of several approved feedstocks under the ethanol programme, was priced under the same govt pricing framework as other approved feedstocks, and was not accorded any special treatment. It said FCI rice accounted for just 0.02% of ethanol production in ethanol supply year (ESY) 2023-24, with its share rising to 24.6% in ESY 2025-26 only after surplus stocks became available. During the same period, maize's share declined from 42.6% to nearly 36%, indicating that distilleries switch between approved feedstocks depending on availability.The ministry also said the programme utilises damaged grain, broken rice and foodgrain unfit for human consumption that would otherwise deteriorate in storage. It added that India is expanding production of second-generation ethanol from agricultural residue under the Pradhan Mantri JI-VAN Yojana to further reduce dependence on foodgrain-based feedstock.Rejecting the contention that ethanol blending survives on taxpayer subsidy, the ministry maintained that the objective of the programme was not to make petrol cheaper on a day-to-day basis but to shield consumers from sharp swings in global crude prices while reducing dependence on imported crude oil, imports of which meet nearly 88% of India's requirement. "Ethanol blending is an insurance policy against global oil shocks and not a day-to-day price competition," it said.
Article Summary: Petrol was projected to cost around Rs 125 per litre in Delhi when global crude prices touched $135 a barrel if India had not blended ethanol with petrol. 20% of every litre comprised domestically produced ethanol procured at pre-agreed prices, insulating retail fuel prices from global crude price spike.

Article Title: TASMAC corruption case: Supreme Court grants DMK's Senthil Balaji interim protection from arrest
