NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Friday granted interim protection from arrest to DMK leader and former Tamil Nadu minister V Senthil Balaji in the alleged TASMAC corruption case. The court directed Balaji to deposit his passport, cooperate with the investigation and refrain from influencing witnesses while granting him relief.A Bench of Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi stayed the operation of FIR No. 05 of 2026 and issued notice to the Tamil Nadu government on Balaji's plea challenging the Madras high court's refusal to grant anticipatory bail."Subject to the petitioner fully cooperating with the probe, his arrest shall remain stayed. He is directed to deposit his passport with the Investigating Officer. FIR No. 05 of 2026 dated July 8 shall remain stayed. He shall not attempt to influence witnesses," the Bench directed, ANI reported.The FIR was registered by the Directorate of Vigilance and Anti-Corruption (DVAC) following the Madras high court's refusal to grant anticipatory bail to Balaji in the alleged TASMAC scam involving purported irregularities in the allotment of liquor shops and bars.During the hearing, the Supreme Court questioned whether the police should have conducted a preliminary enquiry before registering the FIR, observing that it appeared to be based largely on an affidavit filed by the Enforcement Directorate (ED).The Bench also noted that the allegations primarily related to the period between 2020 and 2021 and observed that Balaji was no longer a minister."He is no longer a Minister," the Court remarked, adding that "if an independent investigation found him guilty, he is bound to face consequences."Senior advocate Amit Anand Tiwari, appearing for Balaji along with senior advocates Kapil Sibal and Mukul Rohatgi, argued that custodial interrogation was unnecessary."Our contention is that the FIR is for the incident said to have taken place between 2021 and 2025. I am at no flight risk; no custodial interrogation required. I was the minister in the department and TASMAC is a corporation independent in existence and functioning," Tiwari submitted, according to PTI.Balaji also contended that the FIR substantially reproduced the Enforcement Directorate's affidavit and petition filed before the Supreme Court."In fact, the FIR itself at various places says that it is from the counter affidavit and petition of the ED," his plea stated.Opposing the plea, the Tamil Nadu government argued that Balaji continued to wield considerable influence despite no longer holding office."From 2021 to 2025, he was in power and did not let any complaint sustain against him. We will have a problem if the evidence goes away. Considering the kind of scam that has happened and his antecedents--there are at least six serious cases," the prosecution submitted.The State further argued, "Even if he is not in power, he is able to carry on the influence."Justice Bagchi, however, said the State's concerns could be addressed by imposing appropriate safeguards."He is not going to abscond, as you say. We will ensure that he does not abscond, participates in the investigation and does not interfere with the probe. If there is any breach, we will interfere," Justice Bagchi observed.Chief Justice of India Surya Kant also stressed that the investigation should proceed independently."Hold an independent probe. If he is guilty, he will face..." the Chief Justice observed.While granting interim protection, Justice Bagchi cautioned Balaji's counsel that any violation of the conditions would invite immediate action.The Supreme Court's order came a day after senior advocates Kapil Sibal and Mukul Rohatgi sought an urgent hearing, arguing that Balaji faced imminent coercive action following the Madras high court's refusal to grant anticipatory bail.The case stems from allegations of a large-scale cash kickback scheme in TASMAC involving the allotment of liquor shops and bars.
Article Summary: V Senthil Balaji granted interim protection from arrest in alleged TASMAC corruption case. The court directed Balaji to deposit his passport, cooperate with the investigation and refrain from influencing witnesses. The case stems from allegations of a large-scale cash kickback in the allotment of liquor shops and bars.

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Friday granted a divorce to Jammu and Kashmir chief minister Omar Abdullah after being informed that he and his estranged wife Payal Abdullah, had resolved their matrimonial dispute through mediation.The top court took note of submissions by senior advocate Kapil Sibal, appearing for Omar, that both parties had reached a settlement and filed an application under Article 142 of the Constitution seeking dissolution of their marriage by mutual consent."We will make it a part of our order and will dispose of it in terms of that," a bench of Justices P S Narasimha and Alok Aradhe said, adding that it would pass a formal order, PTI reported."Both of them have embraced freedom. Your lordships may grant divorce," Sibal told the court.When the bench asked when the application had been filed, it was informed that it was submitted on July 22. It is all set out (in the application)," Sibal added.The bench was hearing two petitions, including Omar Abdullah's appeal seeking divorce on the ground of cruelty.In July 2024, the Supreme Court had sought a response from Payal Abdullah after Omar challenged the Delhi High Court's refusal to grant him a divorce.The Delhi High Court, on December 12, 2023, upheld a 2016 family court order dismissing his divorce plea, holding that he had failed to prove allegations of cruelty or desertion against his wife.Before the family court, Omar Abdullah had argued that the marriage had irretrievably broken down, stating that the couple had not shared a conjugal relationship since 2007 and had been living separately since 2009. He and his estranged wife Payal Abdullah, had resolved their matrimonial dispute through mediation. The top court took note of submissions by senior advocate Kapil Sibal that both parties had reached a settlement.

Article Title: ‘Normal’ July rain defies forecast of El Nino impact
Article Text:
Monsoon in India (representative image)

El Niño alone can no more explain India’s rain pattern: Experts

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

India’s monsoon has delivered a surprise this July, defying forecasts of below-normal rainfall despite a strengthening El Nino and reinforcing scientists’ warnings that climate change is altering the country’s most important weather system, report Chittaranjan Tembhekar & Gaurav Talwar.As of July 30, India received 270.1mm of rains in July against a normal of 271.9mm, well within normal range. IMD had said July rainfall was likely to be less than 94% of long period average.However, rainfall distribution remained skewed, with central India receiving 29% excess in July while the east & northeast recorded a deficit of 30% and south 28%.The monsoon deficit since June 1 was 14%. The unexpected turnaround in July has eased fears of a big monsoon shortfall but highlighted a new reality: long dry spells interspersed with short bursts of extremely heavy rain capable of triggering floods and landslides.According to a Climate Trends briefing, successive weather systems cut the national rainfall deficit considerably from 40% at the end of June.Scientists say the biggest lesson from monsoon 2026 is that El Niño alone can no longer explain India’s rainfall behaviour.Global warming, warming oceans and changing atmospheric circulation are increasingly interacting with traditional climate drivers, making monsoon forecasts more difficult.“The challenge is no longer predicting how much rain India will receive, but forecasting where, when and how intensely it will fall in a warming climate,” scientists said.Rainfall remained highly uneven. While 16 meteorological subdivisions states recorded normal rainfall in the season and three saw excess to large-excess rainfall, 17 subdivisions remained deficient. Central India was almost normal with a 1% surplus, northwest India had an 11% shortfall, while east and northeast India remained 30% below normal and south India 25% deficient.The findings are particularly striking because the US National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration has projected an 81% probability of a very strong El Niño developing between Oct and Dec — a pattern usually associated with weaker Indian monsoons.Former IMD director general K J Ramesh attributed July’s recovery to abnormal warming over the western Pacific, which spawned successive monsoon systems over the Bay of Bengal, and the increasing influence of Western Disturbances that enhanced rainfall over Maharashtra and Gujarat.“Climate change is reshaping the characteristics of the monsoon, which existing models are failing to take into account,” Ramesh said.Akshay Deoras of the University of Reading said the monsoon rebounded rapidly after an early July lull. He cited Umbergaon in Gujarat receiving 1,064 mm of rain in 24 hours —among the highest daily totals recorded since 1901 — as evidence of intensifying rainfall extremes, adding that climate change appears to be amplifying the monsoon’s internal weather systems.
Article Summary: India received 270.1mm of rains in July against a normal of 271.9mm, well within normal range. But rainfall distribution remained skewed, with central India receiving 29% excess in July while the east & northeast recorded a deficit of 30% and south 28%.

Article Title: Petrol would've hit Rs 125/litre in Delhi without ethanol blend, says govt
Article Text:
The petroleum ministry defended ethanol blending, stating it saved consumers nearly thirty rupees per litre.





NEW DELHI: Petrol in Delhi would have cost around Rs 125 a litre when global crude prices touched $135 a barrel, had oil companies not blended ethanol into the fuel, the petroleum ministry said on Friday, defending the ethanol programme against claims about its costs, food security impact, and alleged taxpayer subsidy.The ministry said consumers instead paid Rs 94.77 per litre, since ethanol — procured domestically at pre-agreed prices — made up 20% of every litre and helped insulate retail prices from the crude spike, saving nearly Rs 30 a litre at the peak of the crisis.The government held petrol and diesel prices steady for nearly 75 days after the West Asia conflict began on February 28, before raising them by Rs 7.5 a litre in May. Standard E20 petrol (91-octane) now costs Rs 102.12 a litre in Delhi, while 100-octane petrol is priced at Rs 169.The ministry also denied allegations that foodgrain meant for the poor was being diverted for ethanol production, or that subsidised FCI rice was being used to support the programme.On the question of fuel efficiency, the road transport ministry — citing a study by ARAI, SIAM and IOC — told the Lok Sabha on Thursday that BS-III, BS-IV and BS-VI vehicles designed for E10 fuel may see efficiency drop by 2-6% depending on vehicle category and age when run on E20.The oil ministry had earlier told the Rajya Sabha on July 20 that the reduction in such vehicles is limited to about 3-5%.Both ministries said the Ethanol Blended Petrol programme was rolled out through a phased, scientifically validated process, with blending levels raised gradually as production capacity and infrastructure were built up. Road transport minister Nitin Gadkari told the Lok Sabha that the shift to E20 followed validation of fuel systems, engine durability, drivability, material compatibility and emissions performance, with automakers, oil marketing companies, and the sugar and grain industries consulted throughout.The government added that lab studies and real-world data have shown no adverse impact on vehicle performance from E20 fuel, noting that over 20 crore two-wheelers and 3 crore-plus petrol cars have run on these blends without verified evidence of engine failure linked to ethanol blending.
Article Summary: Petrol in Delhi would have cost around Rs 125 a litre when global crude prices touched $135 a barrel, had oil companies not blended ethanol into the fuel. The petroleum ministry said consumers instead paid Rs 94.77 per litre, since ethanol made up 20% of every litre and helped insulate retail prices from the crude spike. The government held petrol and diesel prices steady for nearly 75 days after the West Asia conflict began.

Article Title: ICMR hands over homegrown cervical pre-cancer treatment, vaccine technologies to pharma firms
Article Text:
ICMR transfers medical technologies under Patent Mitra Initiative

NEW DELHI: A potential new treatment for cervical pre-cancer and two next-generation vaccines against typhoid and other gut infections have moved a step closer to becoming available in India after the Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) licensed the technologies to Indian pharmaceutical companies. If successful, the indigenous products could improve access to affordable treatment and vaccines while reducing dependence on imported technologies.The technologies have been transferred under ICMR’s Medical Innovations Patent Mitra initiative, which helps convert government-funded research into products that can be developed, tested and eventually brought to the market.Among them is SHetA2, a potential treatment for Cervical Intraepithelial Neoplasia (CIN), a precancerous condition caused by persistent infection with the human papillomavirus (HPV). If left untreated, CIN can progress to cervical cancer, one of the leading cancers among Indian women.Unlike surgery, which is commonly used to remove abnormal cells, SHetA2 is designed to selectively destroy HPV-infected abnormal cells while sparing healthy cells. Scientists believe it could offer women a safer and less invasive treatment option in the future. The technology has been licensed to Emcure Pharmaceuticals for further development, clinical testing and commercialisation.ICMR has also licensed two vaccine technologies developed by its National Institute for Research in Bacterial Infections (NIRBI), Kolkata, to Biological E. One is a next-generation vaccine against typhoid, while the other is designed to protect against typhoid, paratyphoid and Shigella, bacteria that cause severe diarrhoea and other intestinal infections, particularly among children.The vaccine candidates will now undergo further development and evaluation before they can be considered for regulatory approval and public use.Dr Rajiv Bahl, Secretary, Department of Health Research, and Director General, ICMR, said partnerships between researchers and industry are helping move promising discoveries from laboratories to patients while strengthening India’s biomedical innovation ecosystem.The technology transfer is part of ICMR’s broader effort to support indigenous healthcare innovation through patent protection, technology licensing, clinical validation and regulatory facilitation, with the aim of making affordable medicines and vaccines available to patients.
Article Summary: The technologies have been transferred under ICMR’s Medical Innovations Patent Mitra initiative. If successful, the indigenous products could improve access to affordable treatment and vaccines while reducing dependence on imported technologies. Among them is a potential treatment for Cervical Intraepithelial Neoplasia (CIN)

Article Title: Chicken biryani may make it to noon-meal menu at Tamil Nadu schools soon
Article Text:
School education minister A Rajmohan said the govt is considering the demand put forward by teachers





CHENNAI: State government is considering a demand to serve chicken biryani as part of the noon-meal programme in schools, school education minister A Rajmohan said on Tuesday.The proposal was among several demands raised when the minister met representatives of more than 150 teachers’ and non-teaching staff associations in the city. Some associations sought the inclusion of chicken biryani in the menu at least once a week.Other demands included regularisation of part-time teachers, reduction of the qualifying marks for the Teacher Eligibility Test (TET), pay revision for secondary grade teachers and restoration of the old pension scheme.Rajmohan said the petitions submitted by the associations would be digitised using dedicated software to ensure better tracking. The demands would be categorised, and updates on the action taken would be made available to the associations concerned, he added.Representatives of the Tamil Nadu Elementary School Teachers’ Association sought the filling of teacher vacancies from LKG to Class V in model schools.“Our primary demand is to fill vacant teacher posts from LKG to Class V in model schools, which were repurposed from higher secondary schools in 2018-19.While posts for Classes VI to XII have been filled, the elementary sections continue to bear the brunt of the vacancies,” said R Doss, the association’s district general secretary.“A total of 11,773 have been working as part-time teachers under the Samagra Shiksha for 16 academic years in subjects such as physical education, drawing, computer science and sewing, among others. The govt should regularise their services,” said S Senthilkumar, state coordinator of the Tamil Nadu Part-Time Teachers Federation.
Article Summary: The proposal was among several demands raised when the minister met representatives of more than 150 teachers’ and non-teaching staff associations in the city. Other demands included regularisation of part-time teachers, reduction of qualifying marks for the Teacher Eligibility Test (TET) and pay revision for secondary grade teachers.

Article Title: eBay to pay $56 million to settle harassment lawsuit brought by US couple
Article Text:
Ina and David Steiner/Image: Reuters

Allegations of escalating intimidation campaign





Criminal cases and financial settlement





E-commerce company eBay and several former senior executives have agreed to pay $55.7 million to resolve a civil lawsuit filed by a Massachusetts couple who alleged they were targeted in a sustained campaign of harassment and cyberstalking after publishing critical coverage of the company, The Financial Times reported.The case was brought in 2021 by Ina and David Steiner, who run the industry blog EcommerceBytes. Represented by Scalli Murphy Law, the couple’s lawsuit alleged they were subjected to intimidation following reporting that angered senior figures at eBay in 2019.Court filings describe a pattern of harassment that began online and later escalated into a series of disturbing physical deliveries and coordinated actions directed at the couple’s home in Natick, Massachusetts.The Steiners said they received packages containing live cockroaches, fly larvae, spiders, a bloody pig’s head mask, a funeral wreath and a book about coping with bereavement. They also alleged that pornographic magazines were sent to neighbours in David Steiner’s name.According to the lawsuit, their home address was posted on Craigslist in an apparent attempt to encourage strangers to visit the property, while unsolicited food deliveries were repeatedly sent to their residence.Court documents further allege that eBay employees travelled from California to Massachusetts to monitor the couple, follow them in rental vehicles, vandalise their property and attempt to install a GPS tracking device on their car.The alleged campaign followed internal communications in which then-chief executive Devin Wenig reportedly texted a senior executive that it was time to "crush" Ina Steiner and "take her down."The conduct led to criminal charges in 2020 against seven former eBay employees, all of whom were later convicted and sentenced to prison terms ranging from one to five years. eBay also pleaded guilty in 2023 to related criminal charges and paid a $3 million penalty, according to the report.Under the civil settlement, the Steiners will receive $48.7 million from eBay and former employees. The company will contribute a further $6 million to charitable organisations, while Wenig will pay $1 million to a free speech charity established in Ina Steiner’s name.In a statement, eBay said the harassment "was wrong, reprehensible and should never have happened" and acknowledged the "unprofessional tone in internal communications" involving executives linked to the case.
Article Summary: Ina and David Steiner alleged they were targeted in a sustained campaign of harassment and cyberstalking after publishing critical coverage of the company. Court filings describe a pattern of harassment that began online and later escalated into a series of disturbing physical deliveries. Seven former eBay employees were later convicted and sentenced to prison terms ranging from one to five years.

Article Title: China has built a 582-ton giant magnet to help its 'Artificial Sun' confine plasma hotter than 100 million°C
Article Text:
The giant magnet powering China's next-generation 'Artificial Sun'

Why does a fusion reactor need such a massive magnet?

How superconducting technology makes fusion possible

What makes this magnet different from previous designs?

How China's 'Artificial Sun' programme has evolved

When could fusion electricity become a reality?

Why fusion is considered the future of clean energy

China has achieved a major milestone in its pursuit of commercial nuclear fusion by completing the construction and testing of a colossal 582-ton superconducting magnet designed for its next-generation "Artificial Sun" programme, according to Xinhua News Agency. Measuring 21 metres in length, the toroidal-field magnet is the largest of its kind ever built for a controlled fusion reactor. Developed by the Institute of Plasma Physics (ASIPP) under the Chinese Academy of Sciences in Hefei, the magnet is designed to confine plasma heated to more than 100 million degrees Celsius, a temperature around six times hotter than the Sun's core. According to the project's roadmap, the breakthrough is expected to support China's long-term goal of demonstrating electricity generation from controlled nuclear fusion around 2030.The newly completed magnet is a toroidal-field (TF) superconducting magnet, one of the most critical components of a tokamak fusion reactor. Weighing 582 metric tons and stretching 21 metres long, it is larger than any comparable magnet built for a fusion facility.The magnet was developed for China's Burning Plasma Experimental Superconducting Tokamak (BEST) project, the country's next-generation experimental fusion reactor.Engineers completed construction, factory acceptance and full-parameter testing in Hefei, marking one of the biggest engineering achievements in China's fusion programme.Nuclear fusion requires hydrogen plasma to be heated to temperatures exceeding 100 million°C, far hotter than the centre of the Sun. At such extreme temperatures, no known material can physically contain the plasma.Instead, powerful superconducting magnets generate intense magnetic fields that suspend the plasma inside a doughnut-shaped vacuum chamber called a tokamak. The toroidal-field magnet prevents the superheated plasma from touching the reactor walls, allowing fusion reactions to continue safely while minimising damage to the reactor.Unlike ordinary electromagnets, superconducting magnets operate with virtually zero electrical resistance when cooled to extremely low temperatures. This enables them to carry enormous electrical currents while consuming far less energy.China also successfully tested a high-temperature superconducting central solenoid, another key component often described as the "heart" of a tokamak. The central solenoid generates the plasma current needed to initiate and maintain fusion reactions, working together with the toroidal-field magnet to keep the plasma stable throughout the experiment.According to Chinese researchers, the new toroidal-field magnet has a volume approximately 1.3 times larger than the equivalent magnet designed for the international ITER fusion project in France. It also stores three times more magnetic energy, allowing it to generate stronger magnetic fields for plasma confinement.The six-year development programme involved breakthroughs in superconducting conductor manufacturing, structural engineering, cryogenic technology and quench protection. Researchers say the project has resulted in dozens of patents and new industry standards for large-scale superconducting magnet technology.China's Experimental Advanced Superconducting Tokamak (EAST), widely known as the "Artificial Sun", has already achieved several world records by sustaining ultra-hot plasma for increasingly longer periods. EAST serves as a research platform where scientists test technologies required for future commercial fusion reactors.The newly completed magnet is intended for the BEST reactor rather than the current EAST machine. BEST aims to move beyond laboratory experiments by demonstrating sustained burning plasma and eventually producing electricity from controlled nuclear fusion.China expects construction of the BEST experimental reactor to be completed by 2027. If development progresses as planned, researchers hope to demonstrate electricity generation from controlled fusion by around 2030.Although commercial fusion power remains one of the world's greatest scientific and engineering challenges, each advance in superconducting magnet technology brings researchers closer to producing a virtually limitless source of clean energy with minimal long-lived radioactive waste and no carbon emissions during operation.Unlike conventional nuclear fission, which splits heavy atoms to release energy, nuclear fusion combines light hydrogen isotopes to produce enormous amounts of power. The process generates no greenhouse gas emissions during operation and produces significantly less long-lived radioactive waste than existing nuclear power plants.Scientists around the world consider fusion one of the most promising long-term solutions to growing global energy demand. China's latest achievement demonstrates the rapid pace of progress in the global race to make fusion a practical source of electricity, bringing the vision of an "Artificial Sun" capable of powering cities one step closer to reality.
Article Summary: The toroidal-field magnet is the largest of its kind ever built for a controlled fusion reactor. It is designed to confine plasma heated to more than 100 million degrees Celsius. The breakthrough is expected to support China's long-term goal of demonstrating electricity generation from controlled nuclear fusion around 2030.

Article Title: America just got its 'most-expensive' Zip Code, and it beats Miami's 'Billionaire Bunkers' and its ‘neighbour’
Article Text:
California's Billionaires tax hurting, but not stopping real estate growth



Atherton's security tells the 'posh story'



A six-bedroom, nine-bath mansion featuring a theater, a private rose garden, and a spa hit the market earlier this year in Atherton for nearly $32 million. It found a buyer within 72 hours, selling for more than half a million dollars above the asking price. According to a report by Bloomberg, that lightning-fast deal is a testament to the fresh wave of tech riches washing over the San Francisco Bay Area, driven by a booming artificial intelligence industry and blockbuster IPOs. Nowhere is that wealth more pronounced than in Atherton, a longtime billionaires hub that is now experiencing resurgent real estate demand.The town of roughly 7,000 residents has already recorded five property sales of at least $30 million this year, nearing the record six set in all of 2025, according to Compass broker associate Tom LeMieux. Data from PropertyShark shows the median home price in Atherton has surged 20% to almost $10 million in the first half of 2026 compared to the same period last year, allowing the enclave to regain its title as the most expensive US ZIP code from Miami’s Fisher Island. For those unaware, Fisher Island's appeal is said to be also linked to 'scarcity'. The private island, accessible only by ferry, helicopter, or private boat, has a fixed geographic footprint with little ability to add new supply.Miami's Fisher Island neighbors famous ultra-wealthy residential like the Indian Creek Village "Billionaire Bunker". Indian Creek Island, also known as “the Billionaire Bunker,” is a 300-acre, man-made strip of land in Biscayne Bay just north of Miami Beach that has residents include NFL star Tom Brady, Amazon founder Jeff Bezos and President Donald Trump’s daughter Ivanka Trump.Ken DeLeon, a local luxury realtor for over two decades, told Bloomberg that the current demand is among the strongest he has seen in his career, comparing the market's frenzied feel to the peak of the 2000 dot-com era. He estimates that more than 50 homes in the area will sell for at least $10 million this year. Atherton’s heated market offers a stark snapshot of the Bay Area’s increasingly K-shaped economy. While the expanding AI industry creates extraordinary fortunes for founders and investors, the same boom has been used to justify widespread layoffs and has exacerbated affordability challenges for much of the region.California voters are set to decide on a ballot measure in November that would levy a one-time 5% tax on billionaires to help pay for healthcare. While the proposal has sparked concerns over a potential exodus of the ultrawealthy -- with billionaires like Google co-founders Larry Page and Sergey Brin reportedly building stronger ties to other states -- local real estate professionals say many buyers remain grounded in the area. Luxury real estate agent Dana Carmel noted that deep business, family, and social ties to Silicon Valley tend to outweigh broader tax considerations when buyers decide where to purchase a home.The influx of capital is gradually transforming Atherton’s quiet, tree-lined streets, where century-old oaks shade the residences of venture capitalist Marc Andreessen, WhatsApp co-founder Jan Koum, and Golden State Warriors star Stephen Curry. Older ranch homes are routinely being bought as teardowns to make room for modern, sleek mansions. Two years ago, a developer bought a modest ranch house on Mandarin Way for $5.7 million, tore it down, and built a modern five-bedroom estate that quietly sold in April for $31 million.Along with modern architecture comes an unprecedented focus on private security. Dale Buckner, chief executive officer of Global Guardian, revealed to Bloomberg that Atherton is now his company's top ZIP code for residential security nationwide, surpassing both the New York and Washington, D.C. metro areas. Across the town, Global Guardian maintains 60 employees watching clients’ properties 24/7, with some residents converting pool houses or garages into dedicated surveillance stations.Concerns over privacy and security are also pushing more of Atherton’s ultra-luxury transactions into the shadows. Hugh Cornish, an agent at Coldwell Banker Realty, reported that about 24% of homes in Atherton sold off public listings last year, up from 21% the year prior. Furthermore, many high-profile purchases are handled through limited liability companies to shroud the buyers' identities. Property records and state business filings show that the buyer of the $32 million mansion earlier this year was an LLC tied to Multi-Fineline Electronix, a major manufacturer of flexible circuits used in smartphones, wearables, and emerging AI devices.
Article Summary: Atherton, California, is now the most expensive US ZIP code. The town of roughly 7,000 residents has already recorded five property sales of at least $30 million this year. The median home price in Atherton has surged 20% to almost $10 million in the first half of 2026.

Article Title: Goldman Sachs is 'very impressed' with Microsoft, and forecasts 'behind the scenes ...'
Article Text:
How Microsoft overcame the Bear Case



Cautious optimism on AI



Microsoft offered Wall Street its clearest signal yet that its massive capital commitments to artificial intelligence are yielding tangible, diversified revenue streams. The performance sparked a historic rally in the software giant’s equity, driving its sharpest single-day gain in nearly 18 years. The catalyst came as Microsoft reported its fastest acceleration in cloud revenue since 2022. The results demonstrated that its core Azure infrastructure and enterprise AI offerings are expanding rapidly among corporate clients, while management simultaneously signaled a moderation in capital expenditure growth—addressing a key area of investor anxiety over margin compression.In an interview on Bloomberg Television, Goldman Sachs Group managing director and senior equity research analyst Gabriela Borges highlighted the shift in market sentiment. “You’re seeing more breadcrumbs around Microsoft’s ability to pull varying levers on the monetization side that perhaps were not nearly as obvious as before,” Borges said. Following the quarterly report, Borges reiterated her Buy rating on Microsoft while raising her 12-month price target nearly 5% to $640, implying a potential upside of approximately 64% from Wednesday’s closing price. During intraday trading in New York on Thursday, Microsoft shares surged 17% to $457 -- positioning the company for its largest single-day percentage gain since October 2008.At the earnings call, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella said that the company now counted more than 30 million paid users of Microsoft 365 Copilot, the AI assistant sold as an add-on to the ubiquitous Office software. That’s up from roughly 20 million three months earlier.The market reaction represents a potential turning point for Microsoft, which had faced skepticism over the commercial traction of its generative AI portfolio, particularly relative to hyper-scaler competitors.“One of the bear cases on this stock for the last six to 12 months has been that Copilot is not as good a product as it could be,” Borges noted, referencing Microsoft’s flagship suite of AI productivity tools. However, she emphasized that rapid iteration is closing the capability gap, asserting that product quality is improving and expanding user bases are creating a “positive feedback loop” that accelerates model refinement and utility.Borges characterized Microsoft as a compelling “discovery value” opportunity, particularly within an enterprise environment where rival Google-parent Alphabet Inc has secured significant early territory. Alphabet’s Google Cloud division has built strong momentum, with nearly 90% of Fortune 100 companies adopting its enterprise-grade Gemini platform.Addressing this competitive dynamic, Borges observed that Microsoft had essentially been stuck in a “penalty box for a number of quarters,” as institutional investors defaulted to the narrative that Google held a decisive lead in fundamental model performance and enterprise deployment.However, Microsoft’s latest operating metrics indicate that the perceived divide may be narrowing faster than anticipated. The company revealed that Microsoft 365 Copilot has surpassed 30 million paid seats—a substantial increase from roughly 20 million recorded just three months prior.The next 12 months, Borges argued, will likely demonstrate that the competitive gap between the two tech titans “is not as bad as people think it is,” pointing to “pretty significant improvement behind the scenes” in Microsoft’s software stack and enterprise integration.Despite the strong quarterly numbers, Borges acknowledged that large-scale corporate implementation of generative AI tools remains in its initial phases. She described the current corporate experimentation phase as throwing “a lot of spaghetti at the wall in order to find good product-market fit,” but expressed strong conviction that viable, high-ROI enterprise use cases will mature rapidly.Borges cited her firm’s own internal deployment of advanced software tools as a baseline for the broader corporate learning curve.“I have no doubt we will be in a position six months from now, a year from now — even as I reflect back on our own experience at Goldman Sachs over the last 12 months — the progress that we’ve made with being able to see how these tools can actually help in our day-to-day,” Borges said.
Article Summary: Microsoft shares surged 17% to $457 -- positioning the company for its largest single-day percentage gain since October 2008. Goldman Sachs Group managing director and senior equity research analyst Gabriela Borges highlighted the shift in market sentiment. The market reaction represents a potential turning point for Microsoft, which had faced skepticism over the commercial traction of its generative AI portfolio.

Article Title: Meta AI head shares message for Google Cloud head, who announced he is joining ScaleAI; the company Alexandr Wang founded, but left to head Mark Zuckerberg's AI division
Article Text:
Meta AI head

Meta AI head Alexandr Wang’s message to Google Cloud head

What Francis deSouza said on joining ScaleAI

Who is Francis deSouza

ScaleAI’s expansion

Poll Vote & Share your view What aspect of Scale AI mission do you find most appealing with the new CEO? Developing reliable AI systems. Helping enterprises deploy AI responsibly. Driving innovation in AI applications. 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Scale AI has appointed Francis deSouza, Google Cloud’s chief operating officer, as its new CEO. He replaces interim chief executive Jason Droege, who had led the company since founder Alexandr Wang departed in 2025 to join Meta after its $14.3 billion investment in the startup. Meta AI head Alexandr Wang congratulated deSouza on joining ScaleAI. According to a report by Axios, this new hire signals Scale’s ambition to position itself as an enterprise AI company rather than a data management firm. DeSouza, who also served as president of Google Cloud’s security products business, said he was drawn to Scale because enterprises need help turning AI hype into measurable business results. “Organizations understand the value and the potential of AI, but they want help realizing that potential and deploying AI responsibly and reliably,” he told Axios.Following the announcement, Meta AI head Wang shared a message of support for deSouza on social media platform X (formerly known as Twitter). Wang wrote, “Welcome @fdesouza to @scale_AI as CEO! I started Scale a decade ago at 19, and it has grown to be the backbone of the AI world, powering frontier labs, Fortune 500 companies, and the US Government. Francis is an exceptional leader and the right steward. After spending a lot of time together, I have no doubts he’ll take Scale to greater heights.Thank you @jdroege for your leadership as interim CEO.”The exchange highlighted the close ties between Scale and Meta, given Wang’s transition to lead Mark Zuckerberg’s AI division last year.deSouza also shared a post on X about joining ScaleAI as the CEO. “Big News: I’m joining@scale_AI as CEO, starting August 10. Scale sits at a rare intersection, working with the top AI labs to push the frontier while helping enterprises and governments actually deploy AI they can verify and trust. I’m excited to lead a company with a mission to develop reliable AI systems for the most important decisions. More to come,” wrote deSouza.Francis deSouza is a seasoned technology executive who has held leadership roles across cloud computing, cybersecurity, and genomics. Most recently, he served as Chief Operating Officer and President of Security Products at Google Cloud, where he focused on enterprise adoption of AI and cloud services. Before that, he was President and CEO of Illumina, the genomics company, overseeing its global expansion and revenue growth. Earlier in his career, deSouza held senior positions at Symantec and also founded two startups that were acquired by Microsoft and Symantec. He studied computer science and electrical engineering at MIT, earning both bachelor’s and master’s degrees. Now, as CEO of Scale AI, he is tasked with steering the company’s transition from a data-labeling provider to a broader enterprise AI applications firm.The Axios report further highlighted, that Scale AI, originally known for providing data and human evaluations to train leading AI models, has expanded into building AI applications for enterprises and governments, including the U.S. Department of Defense. The company said its applications business is on track to overtake its data business within 18 months. DeSouza emphasized that demand for data labeling, application deployment, and AI infrastructure management will continue to grow as companies uncover new use cases.
Article Summary: Scale AI has appointed Francis deSouza, Google Cloud’s chief operating officer, as its new CEO. He replaces interim chief executive Jason Droege, who had led the company since founder Alexandr Wang departed in 2025 to join Meta after its $14.3 billion investment in the startup.

Article Title: RAI and Google partner to digitise India’s retail sector
Article Text:
Deeper ecosystem digitization



Future of commerce readiness



The Retailers Association of India (RAI) and Google today announced a strategic collaboration to support digital adoption among Indian retailers, with particular emphasis on small and medium-sized retailers. The initiative aims to leverage capabilities across Google’s product ecosystem – including Google Business Profile, Google Ads, Google Shopping, and Google Cloud – to deliver scalable digital solutions and expand digital enablement across RAI’s network representing over 600,000 storefronts nationwide. Under this collaboration, RAI and Google will explore cooperation across three areas:Accelerating digital adoption for small and medium retailers by equipping them with know-how to leverage Google Business Profile and Merchant Center in enhancing online discoverability of their storefronts, and showcasing in-store inventory to drive local traffic and new acquisitions. This will also involve helping small and medium businesses boost their local reach with Google Ads across Google Search, Google Shopping, Google Pay, and Google Maps.Partnering across RAI-led industry summits, executive workshops, and leadership dialogues to equip retailers with insights into emerging consumer behaviors and AI-driven commerce innovations.Kumar Rajagopalan, CEO, Retailers Association of India, said, “Retail success involves the ability for retailers to know their customers, as well as to adopt modern methods, especially digitization.Retailers Association of India believes in creating a level-playing field for all types of retailers, and one part of this is to enable small retailers to adopt technologies that can help them stay relevant to their customers. This initiative between RAI and Google will help in creating capabilities of digitization for retailers across the country.”Shalini Puchalapalli, Managing Director, Google Customer Solutions, Google India, said, “Small and medium retailers are the backbone of Indian commerce. We already see merchants across India using everyday Google tools to connect with local shoppers, and the bigger opportunity lies in making our full ecosystem work together seamlessly for them. Through our collaboration with RAI, we want to help merchants go further – bringing the combined capabilities of Google Shopping, Google Ads, Google Cloud, and Google Pay — underpinned by Google AI — directly into their hands so they can build resilient businesses. ”
Article Summary: The Retailers Association of India (RAI) and Google announced a strategic collaboration to support digital adoption among Indian retailers, with particular emphasis on small and medium-sized retailers. The initiative aims to leverage capabilities across Google’s product ecosystem – including Google Business Profile, Google Ads, Google Shopping, and Google Cloud.

Article Title: Bernie Sanders makes fun of Mark Zuckerberg says how will he feed his family after California's Billionaire Tax, gets 'corrected'
Article Text:
What is California's 5 percent wealth tax driving billionaires out



Mark Zuckerberg to relocate to Florida



Billionaires exodus from California



Senator Bernie Sanders recently took aim at Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg by sharing a post on social media platform X (formerly known as Twitter), joking about how the billionaire would “feed his family” if California’s proposed billionaire tax goes through. “If voters in California approve the 5% billionaire wealth tax in November, Mark Zuckerberg would owe $10.5 billion in taxes & healthcare would be saved for 3 million low-income people. Poor Mr. Zuckerberg would only have $200 billion left to feed his family. How will he survive?” Sanders wrote. The remark was part of Sanders’ broader push to highlight inequality and mock the resistance of tech elites to the one-time 5% wealth tax targeting residents with assets over $1 billion.Sanders’ jab quickly drew responses pointing out Zuckerberg’s immense fortune, estimated at more than $200 billion. Critics noted that the senator’s satirical concern was misplaced, as Zuckerberg’s wealth places him among the richest people in the world. The “correction” underscored Sanders’ rhetorical style of exaggerating billionaire struggles to emphasize the gap between ordinary families and tech moguls.The trigger linking Thiel to Google's founders is a November ballot initiative in California. Proposed by a healthcare union, it would apply a one-time 5 percent tax on the assets of anyone in the state worth more than a billion dollars. If passed, it would retroactively cover anyone who lived in California as of January 1, with five years to pay.That prospect has already reshaped where some of America's richest people park their money. Larry Page and Sergey Brin, who founded Google in 1998 and turned it into a nearly $4 trillion company, have both been cutting ties with the state that made them. More than 45 California LLCs tied to Page filed last month to go inactive or move out, while an entity connected to Brin terminated or relocated 15 companies in the 10 days before Christmas, the NYT found. A trust linked to Page also picked up a $71.9 million mansion in Miami.Thiel started seriously eyeing Buenos Aires real estate about a year ago, around the time the California measure began gaining attention. He's a veteran at collecting fallback options. Born in Germany and raised in the US, he took New Zealand citizenship in 2011 and applied for a Maltese passport in 2022.Earlier this year, it was reported by Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg is planning to relocate to Florida. A WSJ report revealed that Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg and his wife, Priscilla Chan, are the latest California billionaires to buy a home in South Florida. The couple reportedly purchased a completed waterfront mansion on Miami’s Indian Creek, as per sources with knowledge of the transaction.As to those wondering what gives Florida's Indian Creek 'Billionaire Bunkers' title: It is the residents. The gated man-made barrier island Indian Creek boasts of several billionaires as its residents. Indian Creek Island operates as an independent municipality with its own government and private police who patrol by air, water, and sky. It reportedly has 41 lots and 84 residents. The names include Amazon founder Jeff Bezos, popular investor Carl Icahn and billionaire auto dealer Norman Braman. Google founders Lary Page and Sergey Brin too are said to have bought properties in Florida.As to those wondering what gives Florida's Indian Creek 'Billionaire Bunkers' title: It is the residents. The gated man-made barrier island Indian Creek boasts of several billionaires as its residents. Indian Creek Island operates as an independent municipality with its own government and private police who patrol by air, water, and sky. It reportedly has 41 lots and 84 residents. The names include Amazon founder Jeff Bezos, popular investor Carl Icahn and billionaire auto dealer Norman Braman. Google founders Lary Page and Sergey Brin too are said to have bought properties in Florida.Facebook founder Zuckerberg is not the only billionaire to descend on Miami as California proposes a 5% billionaire tax. While some billionaires including Donald Trump's AI Czar have been open about leaving California, others have been largely discreet. Other than Google founder Larry Page and Sergey Brin, billionaires who have shifted base from California include Oracle co-founder Larry Ellison and PayPal/Palantir co-founder Peter Thiel.What makes Florida attractive for billionaires is that it offers no state income tax. Danny Hertzberg, a Miami real-estate agent at Coldwell Banker Realty, told WSJ that the 5% tax in California is really driving out people in a major way.The 5% tax in California has been proposed by SEIU-United Healthcare Workers West. The workers body is said to be circulating petitions to put the tax on the November ballot. The estimated $100 billion produced by the tax would replace funds hospitals were getting before the federal government tightened enforcement of eligibility requirements for subsidized health insurance.
Article Summary: The Meta CEO and his wife, Priscilla Chan, are the latest California billionaires to buy a home in South Florida. The couple reportedly purchased a completed waterfront mansion on Miami’s Indian Creek, as per sources with knowledge of the transaction. The gated man-made barrier island Indian Creek boasts of several billionaires as its residents.
